_anonymised_copy: Anonymised copy of a registered protocol file: internal provenance fields (storage ids, hosts, resource accounting, internal review notes) were removed or redacted. Embedded sha256 values refer to the original registered file and do not match this copy.

status_at_amendment.done: R2 sample (n = 2,000, sha256 76139c3d9c4d151ad72fa45343670aea8651fe83fd8acff2aba395b29c5e98da) and rewrite pool (n = 600, sha256 a8cfd6a011f4bf63720b21552f13537ea1a6de280d94855f9f237ebf10f168ff) drawn from quid + qtype only, per the registered recipe; attempt-1 prompt file written; generator weights downloading (CPU job); review-kit builder and rescoring script drafted; rescoring script tested on R1 data and synthetic data only

changes.human_review: SINGLE-ANNOTATOR RANDOM AUDIT, not full verification. One annotator (an author) reviews only rows 1-100 of the R2 review sheet (review ids S001-S100). The sheet's fixed random order (numpy default_rng(20261029).permutation over the judge-accepted quids in ascending order) makes these 100 rows a simple random sample of the judge-accepted rewrites. If fewer than 100 rewrites are judge-accepted, all rows are audited. Kit instructions say: review rows 1-100 only, single annotator.
changes.PRIMARY_set: all judge-accepted R2 rewrites (mechanical checks + judge). H1-H3, bootstrap (B = 10,000, seed 20261029, one-sided p = share of bootstrap means <= 0), Holm over the three and the CONFIRMED / NOT_CONFIRMED labels are unchanged. This replaces the rule's 'judge-accepted AND human-confirmed' PRIMARY set; the rule's SENSITIVITY set (all judge-accepted) becomes the PRIMARY set.

audit_analyses_registered.a_acceptance: human acceptance rate among the audited rows: accepted iff same_answer_set = Y AND same_constraint_time = Y; 'unsure', N or blank = not accepted; Wilson 95% interval (z = 1.959964) for the acceptance rate and for the rejection rate (1 - acceptance)
audit_analyses_registered.b_tipping_point: for each k separately: order the PRIMARY questions by d_i = drop(G_k)_i - drop(P_k)_i descending (ties by quid ascending), i.e. those where G drops while P does not first; remove the top m questions from the k-th test only (the other two tests keep the full PRIMARY set), recompute the one-sided bootstrap p of H_k (same B and seed) and the Holm adjustment over the three; m* = the smallest m (scanning m = 0, 1, 2, ...) at which the Holm-adjusted p of H_k is >= 0.05. Report m* and m*/n. Label AUDIT_ROBUST iff m*/n > the upper Wilson 95% bound of the audit rejection rate, else AUDIT_SENSITIVE. If H_k is NOT_CONFIRMED on the full PRIMARY set, m* = 0 and the label is NOT_APPLICABLE.
audit_analyses_registered.c_audited_subset: H1-H3 statistics re-estimated on the audited rows minus the rows not accepted (descriptive only; same bootstrap; no labels used for any claim)

changes.secondary_descriptive: unchanged, computed on the PRIMARY set; the R1+R2 pooled estimate uses the 569 R1 judge-accepted rewrites unless R1 human-review sheets are supplied (stated in the output)
changes.paper_wording: 'human-audited (one author, random 100)'; the R2 rewrites are never described as human-verified
changes.blinding: unchanged: no Hits/accuracy on R2 originals or rewrites until the analysts sends the returned audit sheet; all R2 prediction files are frozen by sha256 before that
